cases.excerpt: We analyzed plasma concentrations of betaine, choline, cysteine, methionine, methylmalonic acid (MMA), vitamin B2, and vitamin B6 in 561 cases and 1,034 controls matched for age and recruitment date, nested within the population-based Northern Sweden Health and Disease Cohort.

effect_size.excerpt: The relative risks for a doubling in concentrations were 1.46 [95% confidence interval (95% CI), 1.04-2.05; P(trend) = 0.03] for choline, 1.11 (95% CI, 1.00-1.23; P(trend) = 0.04) for vitamin B2, and 0.78 (95% CI, 0.63-0.97; P(trend) = 0.03) for MMA. Concentrations of betaine, cysteine, methionine, and vitamin B6 were not associated with prostate cancer risk.

studies.Title: Dietary intake of B vitamins and methionine and prostate cancer incidence and mortality.
studies.Reference: Dietary intake of B vitamins and methionine and prostate cancer incidence and mortality.
studies.Timing: Recruitment from 1990 to 1994 with 15 years of follow-up on average
studies.Population: Men in the Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: The Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study recruited 41,514 people aged 40-69 years between 1990 and 1994. During follow-up of 14,620 men for 15 years on average, we ascertained 1,230 incident prostate cancers and 114 prostate cancer deaths.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: During follow-up of 14,620 men for 15 years on average, we ascertained 1,230 incident prostate cancers and 114 prostate cancer deaths.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: For overall prostate cancer incidence, HRs for riboflavin intake were significantly increased relative to quintile 1 (except quintile 5), with a peak for quintile 3, HR 1.29 (1.07, 1.57).
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: Hazard ratios (HR) and 95 % confidence intervals were estimated using Cox regression. For overall prostate cancer incidence, HRs for riboflavin intake were significantly increased relative to quintile 1 (except quintile 5), with a peak for quintile 3, HR 1.29 (1.07, 1.57).
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: relative to quintile 1 (except quintile 5), with a peak for quintile 3
extraction_supporting_text.timing: recruited 41,514 people aged 40-69 years between 1990 and 1994. During follow-up of 14,620 men for 15 years on average
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: Dietary intakes were estimated using a 121-item food frequency questionnaire

studies.display_only_reason: Eligible study; JBI Fair is below the default pooling threshold.

studies.Population: Black men with histologically confirmed prostate cancer and age- and race-matched controls seen at three major hospitals
